# Humus

> An opinionated Go framework for building services on bedrock's process model. Humus is being rebuilt, package by package, and these pages document what has landed. Releases up to v0.15.0, which pkg.go.dev shows by default, document the Builder/Runner, YAML configuration and rest.Run API that the rebuild removed.

## Docs

- [Humus](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/index.html.md): An opinionated Go framework for building services on bedrock's process model. Humus is being rebuilt, package by package, and these pages document what has landed. Releases up to v0.15.0, which pkg.go.dev shows by default, document the Builder/Runner, YAML configuration and rest.Run API that the rebuild removed.
- [The App lifecycle](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/lifecycle/index.html.md): How humus.Main builds a humus.App, and how the App reads its settings, builds its telemetry and its dependencies, runs its Services, drains and shuts them down within a grace period and turns the outcome into an exit status.
- [Billing job](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/walkthroughs/billing/index.html.md): A walkthrough of a job on humus that bills a month of subscriptions: it issues invoices in PostgreSQL and charges each one through a payments API, once, however often it runs. These pages build it step by step.
- [Serving HTTP](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/http/index.html.md): How to serve HTTP with the httpserver package: an Init that sources httpserver.Settings and returns the Service from NewService, the certificate it requires, the protocols it serves, how it drains and shuts down on httpserver.Main's defaults, what it records, and how to test it with httpservertest.
- [Serving an API with OpenAPI](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/openapi/index.html.md): How to serve an API with the openapi/v3 package: an Init that builds an *openapi.API with NewAPI and serves it with httpserver.NewService, typed paths and parameters, operations and the codecs every body names, jsoncodec and codecs of one's own, streaming ones included, the answers to errors, rejected requests, 404s and 405s, problem details, what happens on a panic or on a failure after the status, security, the OpenAPI 3.2 document, what the API records, how to test it, and what each piece of rest.Run became.
- [Calling HTTP services](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/http-client/index.html.md): How to call HTTP dependencies with the httpclient package: one client per dependency, built in Init from httpclient.Settings sourced with config.Struct, TLS and plain text, which requests are retried and how the end user's Classify decides what an answer means, Retry-After and the timeouts, the circuit breaker and its log records, the body rules, HTTP/2 behind a Kubernetes Service, what it records, and how to test the calls against a fake dependency.
- [Health](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/health/index.html.md): How a humus service reports its health: monitors and how they combine, what liveness and readiness each check, the health Service that owns an App's readiness through the lifecycle, and how httphealth and grpchealth expose the probes to Kubernetes, attached to a server the pod runs or on a probes port, with their answers, manifests, startup probes and tests.
- [Jobs](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/jobs/index.html.md): How to write a job with the job package: a run that job.NewService turns into a humus Service, the exit status Kubernetes sees for each way the run ends, which failures a Job retries, and how the run's span joins the trace of the process that started it.
- [Consuming and producing Kafka](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/kafka/index.html.md): How to consume and produce Kafka with the queue and queue/kafka packages: the contract a Processor keeps, an Init that sources kafka.Settings and returns the Service from NewService, what each Delivery commits and does with an error, how the consumer shuts down and rebalances on humus.Main's defaults, how a Producer built with NewProducer produces dead letters and events, what a call to Produce promises, its delivery timeout, circuit breaker and shutdown, what both record, and how to test them on kfake.
- [Consuming and publishing with RabbitMQ](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/rabbitmq/index.html.md): How to consume and publish with RabbitMQ through the queue and queue/rabbitmq packages: the contract a Processor keeps, an Init that sources rabbitmq.Settings and returns the Service from NewService, what each Delivery acks and does with an error, how the consumer shuts down, rides out a broker's rolling upgrade and turns ready with Consuming, how a Publisher built with NewPublisher publishes with confirms, retries and a circuit breaker, what both record, and how to test an App that uses RabbitMQ, which humus ships no fake broker for.
- [gRPC services](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/grpc/index.html.md): How to serve gRPC with the grpcserver package: an Init that sources grpcserver.Settings, registers generated services on the Service from NewService and returns it, the certificate it requires, what server options can change, how it ends streams and shuts down on grpcserver.Main's defaults, how Kubernetes' probes reach it, how grpcauth authenticates its RPCs, what it records, and how to test it with grpcservertest.
- [Calling gRPC services](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/grpc-client/index.html.md): How to call gRPC dependencies with the grpcclient package: one Client per dependency, built in Init from grpcclient.Settings sourced with config.Struct, TLS and plain text, names and addresses behind a ClusterIP or a headless Service and spreading load with the server's MaxConnectionAge, which calls are retried and how the end user's Classify decides what a code means, the pushback, the circuit breaker and its log records, streams, what it records, readiness with Connected, and how to test the end user's whole App next to a grpcserver backend.
- [Authentication and authorization](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/auth/index.html.md): How a humus service authenticates and authorizes the requests it serves with the auth package: schemes and their typed principals, read with From, requirements and scopes, opening a path with auth.Disabled(), the three places they are enforced, openapi.Security, auth.NewHandler and grpcauth.Interceptors, the answers and WWW-Authenticate challenges, probes left open over HTTP and gRPC, verifying JWTs with auth/jwt on a RemoteKeySet or a KeySet of one's own, answering a *jwt.KeySetError, what humus records, and how to test all of it.
- [Mailer](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/walkthroughs/mailer/index.html.md): A walkthrough of a RabbitMQ worker on humus that sends the emails other services ask for through a provider's API, retries what fails for now after a delay, and dead-letters what never will. These pages build it step by step.
- [The Database resource](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/walkthroughs/databases/resource/index.html.md): The databases controller's custom resource: the Database's spec and status as Go types, its rules, including a CEL rule that makes the name immutable, and the golden CRD reflected from them.
- [The invoices](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/walkthroughs/billing/invoices/index.html.md): The billing job's tables in schema.sql, and the postgres package that issues a month of invoices, reads the pending ones and settles each one once.
- [The topics](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/walkthroughs/orderstatus/topics/index.html.md): The order status processor's four topics: creating them and their ACLs with Kafka's CLI, their keys, their partitions and their retention.
- [The topology](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/walkthroughs/mailer/topology/index.html.md): The mailer's exchanges, queues, bindings and policies in a RabbitMQ definitions file, importing it into the broker, and creating the logins and their permissions with rabbitmqctl.
- [Configuring a humus service](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/configuration/index.html.md): How a humus service's settings get their values: humus packages take plain Go values, and the service's Init sources each one, usually with bedrock's config package, so that a bad value fails startup with exit 78 and an error naming the variable.
- [Telemetry](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/telemetry/index.html.md): How a humus service gets its OpenTelemetry providers: the end user's Builder sources telemetry.Settings and calls telemetry.New, the App hands the SDK to Init, and humus never reads or sets OpenTelemetry's globals.
- [Testing a humus App](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/testing/index.html.md): How to run a whole humus App inside a test with humustest.Start: the App humus.Main would run, under synctest, with no real socket, no file outside the test's temp directory and no secret in the repository.
- [Failure injection](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/failure-injection/index.html.md): How a humus service fails one request on purpose, in production or in a test, with the fault package: turning it on with humus.WithFaults, choosing or writing the codec a scenario travels in, the injection point in every humus client and points of the end user's own, whom each server trusts, the annotation that carries a scenario into a Kubernetes controller's reconciles, which dependencies a scenario goes on to, what a fault does to the retries and the breaker, containing a scenario in production, what it records, and how to test a scenario.
- [Writing a Kubernetes controller](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/kubernetes/index.html.md): How to write a Kubernetes controller with the kube module, on client-go and without kubebuilder: an Init that fills a kube.Connection in a pod or from a kubeconfig and returns the Service from NewController, a custom resource declared as Go values with typed constraints and its CRD kept true to the types by a golden test, a Reconciler handed its object that returns its status, owned resources, finalizers, Kubernetes' own kinds, panics, the settings, leader election and shutdown, readiness, the RBAC a controller needs, what it records, failure injection from an object's annotation down through an operator's controllers, how to test it, and how kubebuilder's pieces map to the module's.
- [Calling the provider](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/walkthroughs/mailer/provider/index.html.md): The mailer's provider package: an httpclient client with a Classify that retries a 409, the request with its Idempotency-Key and API key, what each answer means, Retry-After, and the WireMock mappings that stand in for the provider.
- [Charging](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/walkthroughs/billing/charging/index.html.md): The billing job's payments package: the charge request and its idempotency key, what each answer from the payments API means for the invoice, and the Classify that decides which answers are retried.
- [Order status processor](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/walkthroughs/orderstatus/index.html.md): A walkthrough of a Kafka processor on humus that projects orders' events into their statuses in PostgreSQL, produces each change of status, retries what fails for now through a retry topic, and dead-letters what never will. These pages build it step by step.
- [Talking to PostgreSQL](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/walkthroughs/databases/postgres/index.html.md): The databases controller's admin interface to PostgreSQL: Provision and Drop, the Server that implements them on a pgx pool, their injection points, postgresql:provision and postgresql:drop, and how no credential reaches the SQL text, a span or an error.
- [The projection](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/walkthroughs/orderstatus/projection/index.html.md): The order status projection in PostgreSQL: schema.sql, the events it keeps, and the status folded from them through a state machine, stored in one transaction with the event.
- [Walkthroughs](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/walkthroughs/index.html.md): Example applications that are production-ready, each with pages that build it step by step: the bar every one meets, which its pages close with as a checklist, and the three levels of tests it runs.
- [Databases controller](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/walkthroughs/databases/index.html.md): A walkthrough of a Kubernetes controller on humus that provisions a database and the role that owns it in PostgreSQL for each Database resource, writes the role's credentials to a Secret, and drops both on delete as the Database's deletionPolicy says. These pages build it step by step.
- [Processing a request](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/walkthroughs/mailer/processing/index.html.md): The mailer's Processor: decoding a request, the table that decides what becomes of it, publishing its event with confirms, an event no queue receives, and acking once its result is the broker's.
- [Projecting an event](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/walkthroughs/orderstatus/projecting/index.html.md): The order status processor's Processor: decoding a record, retrying the store's calls, skipping an event already applied, folding the order's history with it, and producing its changes before storing it.
- [Reconciling](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/walkthroughs/databases/reconciling/index.html.md): The databases controller's Reconciler: the password from the Secret, the role and database provisioned, the Secret applied with server-side apply, the Ready condition and its reasons, and rotation by deleting the Secret.
- [The run](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/walkthroughs/billing/run/index.html.md): The billing job's run: it issues a month of invoices, charges every pending one with a bounded number in flight, settles each answer, stops early when every further charge would fail, and returns what the exit status reports.
- [Cleaning up](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/walkthroughs/databases/cleaning-up/index.html.md): How the databases controller cleans up a deleted Database: a finalizer keeps it until the role and the database are dropped, or kept, as its deletionPolicy says, and a failed drop keeps it until a retry succeeds.
- [Init](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/walkthroughs/billing/init/index.html.md): The billing job's Init: its settings, sourced and checked; its secrets, read from files; the pgx pool and the payments client; Faults and the telemetry Builder in Options; and main.
- [Retries and dead letters](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/walkthroughs/mailer/retries/index.html.md): How the mailer parks a request that failed for now in a delay queue, counts its attempts in a header, dead-letters a request that never will succeed with why, and what the queue's delivery limit catches.
- [Retries and dead letters](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/walkthroughs/orderstatus/retries/index.html.md): How the order status processor retries a record that failed for now through orders.retry, with its attempt in a header and a backoff derived from it, dead-letters a record that never will succeed to orders.dlq with why, and what to do with orders.dlq.
- [Init](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/walkthroughs/databases/init/index.html.md): The databases controller's Init: its settings, sourced and checked; its secrets, read from files; the Connection to the API server; the Settings and the Lease; TrustScenario; the Controller; the probes; BuildTelemetry and Faults; and main.
- [Init](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/walkthroughs/mailer/init/index.html.md): The mailer's Init: its settings, sourced and checked; its secrets, read from files; the Publishers and the UserID a parked request carries; TrustScenario; the probes; BuildTelemetry and Faults; and main's grace period.
- [Init](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/walkthroughs/orderstatus/init/index.html.md): The order status processor's Init: its settings, sourced and checked; its secrets, read from files; mTLS to Kafka; the PostgreSQL pool; the two Producers; the probes; BuildTelemetry and Faults; and main.
- [Testing](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/walkthroughs/billing/testing/index.html.md): Testing the billing job: the run as a unit, against a store in memory and a payments API of the test's own; the shared cases and their Target, run in containers and on kind; and the failure injection cases.
- [Deploying](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/walkthroughs/billing/deploying/index.html.md): Deploying the billing job: its image, its CronJob and the kustomization; the kind overlay with PostgreSQL, WireMock and the LGTM stack; and running it on kind, a backfill, and a rehearsal.
- [Testing](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/walkthroughs/databases/testing/index.html.md): How the databases controller is tested: its Reconciler as a unit, on a fake clientset and a fake Admin; the golden CRD; the shared cases and their Target, run in process against k3s and PostgreSQL in containers and on kind; and the failure injection cases.
- [Testing](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/walkthroughs/mailer/testing/index.html.md): How the mailer is tested: its Processor as a unit, on fakes of the provider and the Publishers; the shared cases, their Target and their barrier, run in process against containers and on kind; and the failure injection cases.
- [Testing](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/walkthroughs/orderstatus/testing/index.html.md): How the order status processor is tested: its projector as a unit, on fakes of the store and the Producers; the store against PostgreSQL; the shared cases, their Target and their barrier, run in process on kfake and on kind; and the failure injection cases.
- [Deploying](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/walkthroughs/databases/deploying/index.html.md): How the databases controller is deployed: its image, the kustomization, RBAC, the Deployment and its disruption budget, the grace period, and the kind overlay. Then running it on kind with up.sh, and applying a Database to it.
- [Deploying](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/walkthroughs/mailer/deploying/index.html.md): How the mailer is deployed: its image, the kustomization, the Deployment and its disruption budget, the grace period, and the kind overlay. Then running it on kind with up.sh, and publishing requests to it with mailrequest.
- [Deploying](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/walkthroughs/orderstatus/deploying/index.html.md): How the order status processor is deployed: its image, the kustomization, the Deployment and its disruption budget, and the kind overlay. Then running it on kind with up.sh, and producing an order's events to it with orderevents.
- [Observing](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/walkthroughs/billing/observing/index.html.md): Observing the billing job: a run's trace, records and metrics in Grafana, its dashboard, and what each of its alerts means and asks of you.
- [Observing](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/walkthroughs/databases/observing/index.html.md): What the running databases controller tells you in Grafana on kind: a reconcile's trace in Tempo, its log records in Loki, humus's controller instruments and the containers' restarts in Mimir, the alert rules in deploy/alerts.yaml, the dashboard in deploy/dashboard.json, and the check that Grafana loaded them.
- [Observing](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/walkthroughs/mailer/observing/index.html.md): What the running mailer tells you in Grafana on kind: a request's trace in Tempo, its log records in Loki, the mailer's, humus's and RabbitMQ's metrics in Mimir, the alert rules in deploy/alerts.yaml, and the dashboard in deploy/dashboard.json.
- [Observing](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/walkthroughs/orderstatus/observing/index.html.md): What the running order status processor tells you in Grafana on kind: a record's trace across the topics in Tempo, its log records in Loki, the processor's, humus's, the group's lag and the containers' restarts in Mimir, the alert rules in deploy/alerts.yaml, and the dashboard in deploy/dashboard.json.
- [Production-ready](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/walkthroughs/billing/production-ready/index.html.md): The billing job's production-ready checklist: each item, and how the job meets it, to check a job of your own against.
- [Production-ready](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/walkthroughs/databases/production-ready/index.html.md): The checklist the databases controller meets, and how it meets each item, with the page that builds it. Check your own Kubernetes controller against it.
- [Production-ready](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/walkthroughs/mailer/production-ready/index.html.md): The checklist the mailer meets, and how it meets each item, with the page that builds it. Check your own RabbitMQ worker against it.
- [Production-ready](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-1187/walkthroughs/orderstatus/production-ready/index.html.md): The checklist the order status processor meets, and how it meets each item, with the page that builds it. Check your own Kafka processor against it.
